issues.description: Mandatory author-prepared/custom files and dated checkpoints are consumed but absent from this release; compatible routes and exact field/history contracts remain unverified. Catalog misses do not prove absent access or licenses.
SAS librefs are literal directory placeholders and SAS/Stata handoff paths are Windows C: paths; map these known inputs/outputs to one selected project root before execution.
The SAS startup probe fails during TKELS initialization; SAS runtime, SAS/CONNECT, and WRDS sign-on are unverified. No license absence is inferred.

The supplied workflow is interleaved: SAS creates data_1/data_2; Stata consumes them and exports psm_1st.xpt; SAS consumes that XPORT and produces data_3/data_4; final Stata code consumes those files.
SAS line 2165 says proc sort data=out=tmr_1_0_1; the extra out= makes DATA= malformed. The tmr_1_0_1 producer is immediately above.
SAS lines 1540–1556 open a remote block, then open a second RSUBMIT before closing the first; the a1/z-score producer block needs a matching ENDRSUBMIT boundary before line 1556.
Stata labels Tables 2–7 but has no explicit result export target; use ordinary durable batch/console log capture for each staged Stata segment.

The remote z_score formula uses NI+XINT+TXT and keeps those fields but not OIBDP/DP; local code zero-fills OIBDP/DP and overwrites z_score with (OIBDP-DP)/AT. Confirm the intended formula and field contract before changing it.

evidence.description: Author source evidence: KSVW Datasheet.pdf lines 26-40.
evidence.quote:
1) CDS data: the raw data was obtained from Markit (the first download of this data was
      in the first quarter of 2013). Using the five-year CDS contracts with MR (Modified
      Restructuring) and XR (No restructuring) clauses, we identified the initiation of and
      existence of CDS trading for firms, and certain characteristics such as term count and
      depth. The transformation of raw data to the variables used in the analyses was
      conducted from the beginning of this project. The transformation of CDS data was
      performed mostly by December 12, 2015.

   2) Management Forecasts: the raw data up to 2010 was downloaded from First Call on
      January 17, 2012. Using the quarterly and annual management forecasts issued during
      a fiscal year, we calculated the issuance and frequency of management forecasts. This
      data work was conducted on November 1, 2013. The raw data on management
      forecasts from 2011 to 2014 was downloaded from IBES on November 12, 2015 and
      transformed to the variable used (by calculating the existence and the number of
      forecasts issued during a fiscal year) on November 21, 2015.

evidence.description: Author source evidence: KSVW Datasheet.pdf lines 42-60.
evidence.quote:
3) Firm characteristics: the raw data up to 2014 on financial statement items and stock
      returns/prices from COMPUSTAT and CRSP, analyst coverage from IBES, and
      institutional ownership data from Thomson-Reuters Institutional Holdings (13F) was
      downloaded on November 7, 2015. The transformation of the raw data to the variables
      used in the empirical analyses was conducted mostly by December 12, 2015. Equity
      issuance data up to 2013 was downloaded from Security Data Corporation’s Global

       Issues and transformed on August 23, 2013 and the data up to 2015 was downloaded
       and transformed on October 13, 2015.

   4) The data on board of directors and blockholder ownership up to 2015 from Corporate
      Library was downloaded on December 1, 2016 and was transformed to the variables
      used in the analyses on December 6, 2016.

   5) The data on lending relationships and financial covenants was retrieved from the
      DealScan database (provided by Thomson Reuters Loan Pricing Corporation) and
      processed during the Dec 2015-Jan 2016 period. Credit rating data was retrieved from
      historical S&P and Moody’s credit rating databases and processed during the the Dec
      2015-Jan 2016 period.

actions.description: Resolve the remaining author-specific input contracts and locations before full-pipeline execution.
steps: For R002 and R008, confirm the WRDS COMP.FUNDA_FNCD and TFN.S34 products, expected fields, and historical coverage. The S34 one-row probe timed out; treat the source as unverified, not absent.

Locate or obtain the exact prepared files consumed by the code: raw.Cibeslnk_xpf_2015_01; pay1.rogers_mgmt_forecast; ibes.rogers_forecast_issuance_v_15_11; cds.cds01_14; seo.raw_ver_2013_08; cds.Sdc_equity_issue90to15sep; cds.aud_1_9_ver_2015_11; cds.tmp_1_7_ver_2015_11_21; cds.loans_data; cds.bank_data_may25; acq.tmp_c_4_1_ver_2016_12; cds.Data_blockholding_ver_2017_03_27; cds.tmr_0_4_ver_2016_01_15; and cds.ratings_jan2016.

For each prepared file, preserve the author-provided version and record the fields, key identifiers, types, date bounds, construction steps, and the two-year/rolling-window history required by its linked requirement. In particular, the audit and tmp_1_7 snapshot saves are commented out while the later reads are active; do not assume their WORK predecessors are equivalent.
Treat the catalog matches as discovery evidence only. Do not infer a missing license from catalog absence, and do not rebuild these author-prepared datasets independently.
validation: After an exact candidate file is placed at its mapped path, perform a format-aware bounded readability/field check (SAS reads limited to one row) and verify key/type/date coverage against each linked requirement. Confirm construction provenance for author-prepared snapshots before marking routes compatible.

validation: Check each SAS OUTFILE/libname XPORT path against its consuming Stata use/export path, and check all seven SAS placeholder librefs resolve to the intended input directories before execution.

actions.description: Resolve SAS startup and confirm SAS/CONNECT, WRDS and Stata-export capability in the assigned environment.

Once SAS starts normally, confirm SAS/CONNECT can establish the authorized WRDS session used by SIGNON/RSUBMIT; credentials and service access remain user/site supplied.

Confirm the local SAS host/version has SAS/ACCESS Interface to PC Files support for DTA export. SAS documentation lists DTA as Stata output and recognizes a supported filename extension when DBMS is omitted; this package’s local component/platform capability is still unverified.

Then confirm the actual data_1 through data_4 handoffs are readable as Stata .dta files during an authorized run.

actions.description: Run the author workflow in its supplied SAS → Stata → SAS → Stata order and capture durable logs.
steps: After mandatory inputs, paths, SAS/CONNECT, PC Files export support, psmatch2, and the two SAS source repairs are ready, start the SAS session and run the SAS preparation/construction code through the data_2 export at line 2173. Pause before the XPORT read at line 2178.

In Stata, run the supplied first block through line 130: it consumes data_1/data_2, runs Tables 2–5 and the first PSM stage, then writes psm_1st.xpt. Capture the Stata log/console output for this stage in the configured Results directory.

Resume the same SAS session at the PSM handoff beginning line 2176 so its WORK intermediates remain available. SAS reads IN.PSM_1ST from the XPORT file and exports data_3 and data_4. Keep the SAS log for this stage.

Run the final Stata block at lines 132–144 to consume data_3/data_4 and produce the Table 6/7 results. Capture a durable Stata log/console record in the configured Results directory. Preserve the supplied samples, variables, estimators, and regression statements.
validation: Confirm the files appear in producer order and formats: data_1/data_2 are Stata datasets; psm_1st.xpt is XPORT with dataset PSM_1ST and expected renamed variables; data_3/data_4 reopen in Stata. Inspect SAS/Stata logs for stage completion and retain table output. No successful execution is claimed by this assessment.

actions.description: Resolve the z-score numerator and field handoff with the authors before changing the calculation.

validation: Before analysis, verify that the selected producer supplies every field referenced by the final expression and that the resulting z_score is computed from the author-confirmed numerator; compare intermediate schema and a bounded row check.

A separate z-score field/formula ambiguity is retained for author clarification: the remote query keeps NI/XINT/TXT but not OIBDP/DP, while the local step zero-fills OIBDP/DP and overwrites z_score with the EBIT expression. No formula edit is proposed.

Native, self-written Stata 18 empty-session checks show set memory 4096M is ignored with return code 0 and gen u=uniform()/sort u both return 0 on zero observations. No clean-session repair is warranted; the initial random variable is discarded by the first use, then recreated in the PSM stage.

D0051 was initially suspected to be a SAS7BDAT/XPORT mismatch from the parser target; direct source review confirms the actual handoff is Stata sasxport export to psm_1st.xpt and SAS XPORT libname/read of IN.PSM_1ST. No mismatch is asserted.

The SAS export filenames end in .dta but PROC EXPORT omits DBMS=. Official SAS documentation permits DBMS omission when a recognized extension identifies the format and lists DTA as the Stata format; no DBMS source edit is proposed. Local SAS/ACCESS PC Files license/platform support remains unverified and needs future output-format QA.
